dedupe_keys.name: skyplot dem open source gnss planning and skyplot simulation from digital elevation models

description: SKYPLOT_DEM is an open-source tool for planning and simulating GNSS surveys. Starting from digital elevation models, broadcast or precise orbits and the Keplerian parameters of new constellations such as Galileo, it computes the number of visible satellites, dilution of precision and the error distribution, producing a more realistic skyplot than tools that ignore obstacles such as mountains and buildings. The authors argue that this matters because accuracy depends on seeing at least four satellites and on their relative positions. Producer: Stefano Gandolfi and Luca La Via, published in the journal Applied Geomatics on 18 February 2011. Coverage: any site for which a digital elevation model exists. Access: the publisher page refused the session, so the abstract and licence were taken from the OpenAlex record, which says an open-source software was realised; no download location was read. Licence and cost: article CC BY-NC per OpenAlex; software licence not confirmed, free. Caveats: the tool dates from 2011 and its current availability and constellation support were not checked. Simulation uses: it supports positioning-service planning and exposure of positioning to terrain obstruction. Related record: the G-CAT GNSS coverage analysis tool (model-g-cat-gnss-coverage-analysis-tool).
